extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media researchers, policymakers, news industry professionals and academics
extracted.subtask_description: A global survey-based report summarising how audiences consume and think about online news in 47 countries, including topics such as platform use, trust, misinformation, AI, and payments. The page is the landing/overview for the Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2024 with links to country data, methodology and supplementary analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform importance / platform use for news
rubrics_metrics.description: "The report looks at the growing importance of platforms in news consumption and production, including more visual and video-led social media such as TikTok, Instagram and YouTube.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates how audiences use different social and platform services for news (mentions visual/video-led platforms explicitly). The page highlights country-level differences (e.g., Thailand and Kenya have high TikTok use for news). Use platform-specific measures of reach and usage frequency to assess this dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience attitudes towards the use of AI in news
rubrics_metrics.description: "It explores audience attitudes towards the use of AI in news",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures public acceptance, concerns or expectations about generative and other AI applications in journalism. The site links to a supplementary qualitative report ('OK computer?') and dedicated pieces (e.g., 'Public attitudes about AI and journalism'). Use both survey items and qualitative findings to characterise attitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of creators and news influencers
rubrics_metrics.description: "It explores... the role of creators and news influencers",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the influence, trust and reach of non-traditional news creators and influencers compared with legacy news brands. Consider metrics on audience reliance, perceived credibility, and engagement with creator-produced news content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment for news / willingness to pay
rubrics_metrics.description: "How much do people pay for news? And what might encourage more people to pay?",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks at current payment behaviours and potential motivators for subscriptions or one-off payments. Guidance: compare proportions paying for news, identify incentives that increase uptake, and segment by country and demographic.

rubrics_metrics.name: News avoidance / news fatigue
rubrics_metrics.description: "A 'platform reset' is changing how audiences interact with news, while news avoidance ... have both grown since last year",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures the extent to which people deliberately avoid news or feel worn out by the news agenda (page cites Spain: worn out by news up from 26% in 2019 to 44% in 2024). Use time-series comparisons to capture trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concerns around misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: "... concerns around misinformation have both grown since last year",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures public concern about misinformation/disinformation. Guidance: assess levels of concern, perceived prevalence, and whether concern has increased year-on-year; cross-reference with trust measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in news
rubrics_metrics.description: "How audiences think about trust in news",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores public trust levels in news (e.g., country trust rates such as Hungary and Greece: only 23% trust most news most of the time). Use direct survey questions about trust and analyse by country, platform and outlet type.

rubrics_metrics.name: User needs (audience needs)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigates what audiences want from news services (format, topics, depth, frequency). Guidance: identify unmet needs and preferences to inform product and editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology / sample design
rubrics_metrics.description: "This year's report ... is based on a YouGov survey of more than 95,000 people in 47 countries ... Research was conducted by YouGov (and their partners) using an online questionnaire in January and February 2024.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents sample size, geographic coverage, and data collection mode (online questionnaire). Use methodological notes to judge reliability, representativeness, and comparability across countries; the page links to a dedicated Methodology section for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-level highlights and comparative data
rubrics_metrics.description: "Explore data from your country" and "Highlights from countries" (examples: Hungary and Greece low trust; Spain increased news weariness; Thailand and Kenya high TikTok news use; Argentina falling interest),
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides country-specific metrics and notable trends. Guidance: use interactive tools to build customised charts, compare markets and demographics, and consult the slide presentation and downloadable data for teaching and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary qualitative research on generative AI
rubrics_metrics.description: "Supplementary report: 'OK computer? Understanding public attitudes towards the uses of generative AI in news'. Report commissioned by the Reuters Institute and based on qualitative research by strategic insight agency Craft.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers qualitative insights complementing the main quantitative survey; useful for understanding nuance in attitudes towards generative AI. Guidance: combine qualitative findings with survey results to interpret public opinion.
